summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on the conditions of salah, specifically focusing on the fifth condition of facing the Kaaba. He explains the principal rule: if the Kaaba is visible, one must face it directly; if not visible, one must face its general direction with a permissible deviation of up to 45 degrees. Sh. Ali Mashhour then details three exceptions where facing the Kaaba is no longer obligatory: when a person has no way of knowing its direction, during fear prayer when life is at stake, and when praying optional prayers while traveling. He clarifies the common misconception that travelers can pray obligatory prayers in any direction, emphasizing that only optional prayers have this allowance. Using Quranic verses and hadith from the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the companion Omar, Sh. Ali Mashhour establishes that whoever makes a genuine effort to face the Kaaba according to their knowledge and ability will have their prayer accepted, even if they later discover they faced the wrong direction.
